name: release-notes
description: Write user-facing release notes for the current state of the project: gather the real changes from git, group them into Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed, and save them as a reviewable file.
author: jarvis-os

steps.title: Inspect the recent history: run git_diff and read the recent commit subjects to build the real list of changes since the last release tag (git tag --sort=-creatordate lists it, if tags exist)
Read any existing CHANGELOG.md or RELEASES.md to match the project's established format and avoid duplicating already-released entries
Group the changes into Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed, written user-facing (what a user notices, not commit jargon); drop pure-revert pairs and internal-only churn
Write the notes to RELEASE_NOTES.md in the project root with a suggested version heading, a one-line summary at the top, and each group as a section; if the user supplied a version, use it
Verify every claim: re-read RELEASE_NOTES.md and confirm each bullet traces to a real commit or diff you saw; correct or delete anything you cannot trace

validation: RELEASE_NOTES.md exists in the project root, starts with a version heading and a one-line summary, and every bullet traces to a real commit observed in step 1
expected_output: RELEASE_NOTES.md with version heading, summary line, and Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed sections of user-facing bullets
failure_recovery: if there is no git history or no changes since the last tag, say so and write notes covering the current diff instead; never invent changes
